claims.head: Buckle up
claims.call: The game’s pace score is above 106, faster than either team’s usual.
claims.see: More than 70 shots between them at 5-on-5, on goal or wide, which usually means 57 or more shots on goal on the scoreboard.
claims.body: The Maple Leafs play some of the league’s fastest games, and so do the Flames. We think this one runs hotter than either team’s usual.

claims.head: Depth against star power
claims.body: On depth, Calgary is one of the league’s best, but Toronto is one of the worst. If this one comes down to the bottom six, that suits the Flames.

notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 21% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the lowest share in the league (a typical team: 43%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

John Tavares is out week to week (lower body injury) and has missed the last 4 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters.

CGY.head: Not an easy night for the Flames
CGY.body: Calgary has home-ice advantage, but Toronto has been out-chancing opponents lately. The Flames’ best way through is piling up shots.

TOR.head: The Maple Leafs should have the upper hand
TOR.body: Calgary has home-ice advantage, but Toronto has been out-chancing opponents lately. The Flames can make it interesting if they keep the shots coming.

items.text: William Nylander has a point in six straight games against Calgary, and 15 points in his last six against them.
The Maple Leafs are newly without Nick Blankenburg, and have been without Chris Tanev and John Tavares for several games.
The Flames have been without Samuel Honzek, Joel Hanley and Connor Zary for several games, and have had to make do without Jonathan Huberdeau all season.
